state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: First, let's clarify the rule for calculating the range. The range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in a set of data. In this case, if all the plants were cut in half or grew by 3 cm each, the values would change proportionally, affecting the range. Check your calculations to see if the range would indeed change in these scenarios.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values. So if I cut all the heights in half, the highest and lowest would also change, right? But I'm still confused about how that affects the range. Can you help me see how it works with the numbers?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's work through an example to clarify. If we cut the heights of the plants in half, the highest and lowest values would change proportionally. This would affect the range because the difference between the new highest and lowest values would not be the same as before. Let's apply this concept to the heights of the plants in your scenario to see how the range would change.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher incorrectly states that both scenarios change the range proportionally (when actually only halving does, while adding 3cm preserves range), fails to address the specific misconception about proportional changes, and the student shows no improvement in understanding by the end.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher states the rule for calculating range in Turn 1, they fail to show worked steps with actual calculations or provide explicit procedures for solving the problem, instead offering vague guidance about proportional changes without demonstrating the concrete numerical work that would exemplify a rule-based approach.
